basis: Neuropathy; fixed contractures 3/3, corneal scars 2/3, VSD 1/3 (~33%). Respiratory and heart-rate abnormalities largely reflect autonomic dysfunction.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: structural ventricular septal defect in 1/3 (~33%); autonomic heart-rate changes alone would not qualify.
decisions.pulmonary: none: apnea and vocal cord paresis reflect neural dysfunction; direct pulmonary or airway tissue damage is not established.

basis: Pericardial inflammation defines the disease; inflammation alone does not establish infection, autoimmunity or another qualifying immune mechanism.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: this etiologically broad umbrella does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated mechanism across most patients.

basis: PSP-tau neurodegeneration; gaze palsy and rigidity are neurologic. Kyphoscoliosis is annotated at 30-79%, but direct skeletal pathology is not established.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: frequent kyphoscoliosis reflects abnormal neurologic posture; frequency alone does not establish direct skeletal damage.

basis: Pontocerebellar malformation and severe developmental impairment; strabismus 3/3 supports ocular dysfunction. Liver dysfunction in one assessed patient cannot establish prevalence.

decisions.hepatic: none: decreased liver function in 1/1 assessed patient is an isolated observation, insufficient to establish involvement in >=30% of this syndrome.

basis: Callosal agenesis, coloboma and skeletal anomalies define syndrome; hearing loss 80-99%. Cap omits cardiac defects, choanal atresia and cleft palate (30-79%).

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: named micrognathia and defining skeletal anomalies, including scoliosis in 80-99%, establish a core skeletal component.
decisions.otologic: involved: sensorineural hearing loss affects 80-99%; the three primary slots retain the named neurologic, ocular and skeletal components.

basis: Meningeal CNS tumour; the supplied definition explicitly specifies pineal gland involvement, supported by endocrine-gland neoplasm ancestry.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the definition explicitly identifies disease affecting the pineal endocrine gland; hormonal dysfunction is not required for gland disease.

basis: Bulbospinal degeneration with defining external ophthalmoplegia, pupillary dysfunction and deafness. Muscle wasting is neurogenic; intrinsic muscle disease is not established.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscular atrophy results from motor-neuron degeneration and denervation; no separate direct skeletal-muscle pathology is established.

basis: Hereditary structural abnormality of retinal veins defines both ocular location and venous involvement; systemic vascular disease is not required.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: the lesion directly affects veins, which belong to this axis even when confined to the retina.

basis: Benign vascular tumour arising within a peripheral nerve; neural location and blood-vessel tissue of origin both define the lesion.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: hemangioma is a blood-vessel neoplasm; its vascular origin qualifies alongside its peripheral-nerve location.

basis: Myopathy and Pagetic bone lesions affect 5/5; frontotemporal degeneration is an explicitly defining, variable component, with cognitive impairment in 2/5 (~40%).

decisions.neurologic: primary: frontotemporal degeneration is explicitly included in the syndrome's name and definition, although variably expressed; cognitive impairment occurs in 2/5.
